note: Independent rejudgment after rereading RFC 4271 Sections 8.1.2, 8.2.1.5 and 8.2.2 Idle, all eight current tagged units and their assertion-producing helpers, and the reached FSM, Session and Peer start producers. Idle Event 3 resets counter 7 to exactly zero in active and passive modes; Event 6 and Event 3 outside Idle retain counter/state. Real Peer positive cycles start a new useful connection after Established exits by received Cease or actual HoldTimer expiry and observe counter 1 before restart and exactly zero after the new OPEN. Failed OpenSent attempts preserve exactly one across a next dial, including an unsuccessful cycle following an earlier Established cycle; these distinguish resetting every cycle from consuming the prior Established result once. Real inbound-notify controls hold actual backoff and prove the new socket reaches OpenSent with zero after actual HoldTimer expiry, versus one after a never-Established failure. The passive positive observes exact leave-Established count one and a distinct Active Session with zero after Cease, real expiry or automatic teardown; its teardown helper verifies Cease and ErrTeardown. Peer.runOnce consumes cycleReachedEstablished with Swap(false), defaults to the damped start, selects the automatic start after Established, and overrides only the first operator cycle. Its factory attaches the peer-owned counter before any start. Removing the unused emitFSMEvents event argument does not change this selection or any test assertion. RFC 4271 Section 8.2.1.5 says, "The details of these actions are outside the scope of the FSM document." Initialization is observed through creation and use of each next connection/Session, not an invented exhaustive resource inventory. The current short and derived row contain no gap or partial annotation and the derived row lists all eight covers. Runtime discrimination freshness is checked separately before stamping this reread; this note claims no new execution.
